title: Tensor insertion across quotient coefficient systems
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $S_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$ and $R_W=\lim_n S_{W,n}$ for $W=X,Y$, with projections $\pi_{W,n}$ and quotient maps $\rho_{W,n}:S_{W,n+1}\to S_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use $G=g^{-1}$ with structure isomorphisms $c_R:GR_Y\to R_X$ and $c_n:GS_{Y,n}\to S_{X,n}$ [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]; thus $\pi_{X,n}c_R=c_nG\pi_{Y,n}$. A complex means an unbounded cochain complex of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $(M_n,w_n)$ be any strict system [def-weil-inverse-system] of $S_{Y,n}$-complexes with $\rho_{Y,n}$-linear chain maps $w_n:M_{n+1}\to M_n$. Put $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_{\pi_{X,n}}(GM_n\otimes_{GS_{Y,n},c_n}S_{X,n})$, using sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Give $GM_n$ its $R_X$-action through $c_R^{-1}$ and $G\pi_{Y,n}$. Let $j_n:GM_n\to C_n$ be the actual sheafified insertion $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. The presheaf maps $x\otimes b\mapsto G(w_n)(x)\otimes\rho_{X,n}(b)$ respect balancing and restrictions and induce $R_X$-linear chain maps $v_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$; the maps $j_n$ are $R_X$-linear chain maps and satisfy
$$v_nj_{n+1}=j_nG(w_n).$$
For any map $f_\bullet:M_\bullet\to M'_\bullet$ of such systems, the maps $f_n^g=G(f_n)\otimes1$ commute with $v_n$, and
$$f_n^g j_n(M)=j_n(M')G(f_n).$$
If $P$ is any $R_Y$-complex with $R_Y$-linear maps $r_n:P\to M_n$ satisfying $w_nr_{n+1}=r_n$, then $\theta_n=j_nG(r_n):GP\to C_n$ is $R_X$-linear and $v_n\theta_{n+1}=\theta_n$, with $GP$ carrying the transported action through $c_R^{-1}$. All equalities are equalities of the specified sheafified chain maps before localization; no K-flatness or boundedness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Use the existing finite comparison complex and its formula on every inverse-image section. Repackage its underlying abelian sheaf maps as completed-linear maps: the projection equation for the completed coefficient comparison gives pi_Y,n(c_R^{-1}(a))=c_n^{-1}(pi_X,n(a)), and finite linearity supplies the required scalar equation. The differential equation is the finite comparison chain-map equation. Its formula on every section gives uniqueness of insertion.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sectionwise tensor and change of rings; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), factorization and uniqueness

proof.text: The site postcomposition/pullback adjunction for the scheme isomorphism is an equivalence. The constant coefficient comparison is the mate of the direct ring map, so that direct ring map is invertible. Transport module actions along the site equivalence and this ring isomorphism using Mathlib SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence. Thus finite module direct image is an equivalence; its adjunction unit is invertible. Restriction along the canonical comma arrow is invertible as well. Their composite x to x tensor 1 is therefore bijective on every section. The insertion formula now shows insertion is an isomorphism of complexes.

proof.text: For arbitrary finite complexes K,L and a completed-linear reduction map w, define v=j_K^{-1} G(w) j_L. Finite comparison linearity gives x tensor b = j_K(c_{n+1}^{-1}(b)x). Coefficient naturality gives rho_Y,n(c_{n+1}^{-1}(b))=c_n^{-1}(rho_X,n(b)); applying the assumed reduction semilinearity of w proves the required formula for v on x tensor b. A competing map agrees after precomposition with the invertible j_K by evaluating its formula at b=1. This proves the exact existence-and-uniqueness statement and identifies the chosen transition.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sectionwise tensor and change of rings; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), factorization and uniqueness

proof.text: Finite comparison naturality gives insertion naturality. The chosen transition formula at b=1 gives j_K v=G(w) j_L, since coefficient reduction preserves 1. Both are equations of completed-linear chain maps because equality is tested on every section in every degree.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sectionwise tensor and change of rings; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), factorization and uniqueness

proof.text: For a system map f, cancel the invertible insertion at the upper source level. Apply insertion naturality, then the insertion-transition equation, apply G to the given commuting square for f and w, then use insertion naturality and the insertion-transition equation in reverse. This proves the transition naturality square. Insertion naturality itself supplies the other required system-map clause.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sectionwise tensor and change of rings; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), factorization and uniqueness

proof.text: Expand augmentation as G(r_n) followed by insertion. Associativity and the insertion-transition equation rewrite its composite with transition as G(r_{n+1}) G(w_n) j_n. Functoriality and r_{n+1} w_n=r_n identify this with the nth augmentation. Assemble these identities into the three conjuncts of quotient_tensor_insertion. No flatness, boundedness, surjectivity, localization, or new auxiliary assumption is used.
